correctness.rationale: For every \(d\ge2\) and each strictly positive directional rate, the \(M\)-matrix inverse is positive and Walsh decomposition gives identical return diagonals equal to the exact subset sum. The crossing is unique because the return decreases strictly from \(1\) to \(2^{-d}<1/2\). A positive-definite Hessian from singleton Bernoulli events yields strict Schur convexity; majorization and monotone crossings give the stated unique extremizers. A leave-one-out convex-order argument proves dimension monotonicity. The centered binomial moment expansion justifies coefficients \(1/2\) and \(5/8\) with \(O(d^{-3})\) remainder. An exact two-branch Bernoulli decomposition at \(s=c/\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) proves the singular coefficient. The full analytical proof does not rely on the 3,474 supplementary checks. No assertion extends to zero rates before the singular limit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 resolvent-return law already proves positivity iff the return resolvent diagonals exceed one-half, so this general reduction is prior art. Karlin–Lindqvist–Yao (1993) already studies hypercube spectra and spectral majorization across Hamming-distance graph families. The new claim is the strict Schur comparison under coordinate-conductance majorization on one cube, the exact all-budget optimization including complete maximizer classification, the two-term dimension law, and the singular small-rate-floor law. An accessible full-text 2007 anisotropic-diffusion paper treats flux limiters, and a full-text 2023 positivity paper treats one-dimensional Dirichlet grids. None of their inspected claims covers this complete result. The inaccessible 1993 full text remains a stated priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: The full 1993 Karlin–Lindqvist–Yao specialist article was inaccessible; a theorem not described by the abstract could overlap the spectral-majorization portion.
The literature on two-state tensor-product Markov chains and isotropic diffusion may contain an equivalent weighted positivity-extremum statement under different terminology.
The generic resolvent criterion and majorization/Jensen proof ingredients are established prior work; only the combined precise cube theorem is asserted as a contribution.

value.rationale: For a natural finite product diffusion network with a fixed total coordinate rate and practical positive rate floors, the theorem exactly solves which allocations maximize or minimize the admissible positivity horizon. It proves a strict design law that the usual spectral upper eigenvalue (fixed at \(2S\)) cannot detect, identifies the unique all-parameter rate extrema, and quantifies both the high-dimensional small correction and a nontrivial inverse-square-root singular boundary. These objects and precise scalings are intrinsically relevant to maintaining nonnegative diffusion states, not arbitrary finite table slices or a mere renaming of a known criterion. The direct general \(M\)-matrix and convexity ingredients alone are not asserted as the value.
